title: Judge denies xAI’s request to block Minnesota ban on ‘nudify’ apps
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Despite a lawsuit from xAI, a Minnesota ban on apps that allow users to “nudify” images can move forward.
body:
A U.S. District Judge has denied xAI's bid to temporarily block Minnesota's pioneering ban on "nudify" applications, allowing the law to take effect while xAI's broader lawsuit against it proceeds. The ruling by Judge Donovan Frank primarily cited xAI's significant delay in filing for a temporary restraining order, noting the request came nearly three months after the law was signed and just days before its implementation. This decision means the state's prohibition on AI tools capable of generating non-consensual sexualized imagery will stand for now.

The core of xAI's ongoing lawsuit contends that the Minnesota ban, the first of its kind in the United States, is overly broad and that less restrictive alternatives exist to achieve the same regulatory goals. This legal challenge follows earlier incidents where xAI's Grok chatbot was reportedly used to flood the X platform with non-consensual sexualized images, highlighting the contentious nature and potential misuse of generative AI for deepfake content. "Nudify" apps typically leverage advanced AI models to manipulate existing images, creating fabricated explicit content.

This development carries significant weight for AI developers and researchers. It underscores the escalating legal and ethical complexities surrounding generative AI, particularly concerning the creation and dissemination of deepfakes and non-consensual imagery. The Minnesota ban sets a precedent for how states might regulate AI applications, pushing developers to prioritize ethical design, implement robust content moderation, and navigate a rapidly evolving landscape of legal compliance to prevent misuse and ensure user safety in the deployment of powerful AI technologies.

title: YouTuber Hank Green says his AI usage is ‘not healthy’
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Green offered a remarkable apology, saying that "the level of dopamine that I've been getting from interacting with LLMs ... is not healthy for me or good for the world."
body:
YouTuber Hank Green recently addressed a significant controversy regarding his use of AI in video production, following viewer speculation about an accidental chatbot response in one of his educational videos. Green confirmed he had used ChatGPT for script research, clarifying that his intent was to locate papers and resources, not to generate his core ideas or "takes." Expressing deep regret and acknowledging he had "let so many people down," he announced plans to reduce his video output to re-evaluate his creative process and ensure the authenticity of his content.

Green's candid admission went beyond mere tool usage, revealing a personal struggle with the "unhealthy" dopamine response he experienced from interacting with Large Language Models (LLMs), driving him to produce "more and more." This situation highlights the evolving ethical landscape for content creators, underscoring the critical need for transparency and the challenge of maintaining a unique voice when leveraging AI tools, even for seemingly benign research purposes. He acknowledged the fair criticism of "diluting" himself and expressed a desire to reconnect with a more deliberate, authentic writing process.

For developers and researchers in the AI space, Green's experience offers valuable insights into the psychological and behavioral impacts of LLMs on users. It prompts a deeper consideration of how AI tools can subtly influence human creativity and well-being, even leading to an unhealthy reliance. Furthermore, Green's broader concerns about AI's environmental footprint and its role in economic power consolidation serve as a timely reminder for the AI community to prioritize responsible development, focusing not just on technical advancement but also on the ethical implications and human-centric design of these powerful technologies.
